archetype.name: Playoff Team (frontcourt-first)
archetype.definition: A team built around an elite big-man core that has won 50-plus games in each of the last four seasons, now starting slowly with its shooting off and its wing rotation unsettled.

report.headline: Shooting slump, shaky wings and elite glass: a contender's noisy start
report.take:
Denver is 1-1, and two games are far too few to rewrite five seasons of evidence. The history is clear. This franchise went 54-28 last year with the league's best offense (Off Rank 1), and it has not finished below 48 wins in the window the sheet shows. The 12th-place site rank and 41-win pace mostly reflect one ugly night in Oklahoma City, an 84-96 loss, followed by a 141-135 overtime win over New Orleans. That gives a differential of -6 and a W vs Pt Diff of exactly 0. There is no luck to strip out, just very little data.

What is driving the early numbers is shooting. Denver's 3P % sits at 29.9 (24th), down from 39.6 last season. That is why an offense that led the league now rates 18th with a 109.7 ORtg. The team is still taking threes at a normal clip (42.5 3PA Rate) and getting to the line more than most (FT Rate 33.7, 7th), so the shot diet looks healthy. The makes have not come. Expect that to correct. The more structural story is the frontcourt, graded A+. Nikola Jokić has 48 points, 22 rebounds and 15 assists in 79 minutes, and Trevon Brazile has pulled down 21 boards off the bench. Behind them the team ranks 4th in ORB % and 2nd in RPG.

The numbers flatter the defense and hide the wing problem. Opponents have shot 27.2% from three, 3rd-best in the league and nearly seven points under the league average. That is almost entirely shooting variance and will rise. The part of the defense Denver controls looks worse. Opponents are finishing 73.8% at the rim (26th) and getting there more often than average, which echoes a defense that ranked 21st in each of the last two seasons. On the wings, the grade is an F. DeMar DeRozan has a -9.8 BPM and a -23.9 On-Off and has hit no threes, and opposing small forwards have scored well above their own averages against Denver (rv 30 on points).

Where this goes: the shooting should return to something like last year's level, and the rebounding edge looks real. The defense will likely settle in the bottom half once opponents' threes start falling. That adds up to a top-eight-ish team again, not a title favorite, unless the wing minutes get sorted out. The schedule this week is soft enough to fix the record quickly.

strengths.title: An A+ frontcourt that dominates the glass
strengths.body: Jokić, Aaron Gordon and Brazile give Denver the league's top-graded frontcourt. The team rebounds a third of its own misses (ORB % 33.3, 4th), well above the league's 27.8. Gordon has been efficient (60.3 TS %), and the group has carried most of the minutes and scoring. The rebounding rate will cool from two games, but a frontcourt this deep should keep it a real edge.

strengths.title: Healthy shot profile despite the misses
strengths.body: Denver is drawing fouls at the 7th-highest FT Rate, up from 29.4 last season, and it is still letting threes fly at a league-average-plus rate. The 29.9% from three is the outlier. The same core shot 39.6% last year, and nothing in the sheet suggests that skill has vanished. When the makes return, the 18th-ranked offense should climb sharply.

strengths.title: Murray stabilizing the backcourt
strengths.body: Jamal Murray leads the guards with 48 points and 8 threes on 55.2 TS %. The team has been 10.2 points per 100 better with him on the floor. The backcourt grades only a C because the minutes behind him have been poor (Tyus Jones -14.3 On-Off). Murray's share of the load should keep that group respectable.

concerns.title: No rim protection, and it isn't new
concerns.body: Opponents are converting 73.8% at the rim, 26th in the league and well above the 66.2 league average, while also getting more of their shots there than average. The 15th-ranked DRtg is propped up by opponents' cold three-point shooting (27.2%, 3rd), which will not hold. With the defense 21st in each of the last two seasons, this looks like a real, ongoing weakness.

concerns.title: The wing rotation is the weak link
concerns.body: The wings grade F. DeRozan has a -9.8 BPM and -23.9 On-Off in 52 minutes, and Bryce Hopkins and Cam Whitmore are also deeply negative. On defense, opposing small forwards have outperformed their own averages by more against Denver than against anyone (rv 30 on points and pra). It is a two-game sample, but if it persists it caps both ends of the floor.

concerns.title: Leaky defensive rebounding
concerns.body: For all the offensive-glass dominance, Denver is grabbing just 70.3% of opponents' misses (DRB %, 20th), below the league's 72.1 and well below last season's 75.3. Opposing centers have averaged 21.5 rebounds against Denver. Brazile's minutes should help, but the drop is worth watching.

trend.note: Two games, two extremes: an 84-point loss at Oklahoma City and a 141-point overtime win over New Orleans. There is no trend yet, just a wide range of outcomes while the shooting settles.

weekAhead.headline: Three soft defenses, then a real test against Portland
weekAhead.body:
The first three games come against some of the worst defenses in the league. Golden State (0-3) owns a 124.0 DRtg (29th), an F-graded frontcourt and the 29th-ranked DRB %. That is an ideal setting for Denver's offensive rebounding and for Jokić. New Orleans (0-3) is 25th in DRtg and has been gutted by centers, giving up 30.67 points a game to the position, worst in the league. Phoenix sits 30th in Net Rtg and DRtg and 30th in DRB %, and opposing point guards have hung 55.5 points a game on it. This is the stretch where Denver's shooting should bounce back and the record should move.

The week closes at home against Portland, 2-0 with the league's best Net Rtg (24.5) and the No. 2 site rank. Portland's defense is 1st in Opp eFG %, Opp 3P % and Opp Rim Rate, so it keeps teams out of the paint. It has, however, given up 24 points a game to centers. Anything less than three wins in the first three would be a disappointment. Portland is closer to a coin flip.

keyMatchups.title: Jokić against the New Orleans middle
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans has allowed the most points, rebounds-plus-assists and pra to centers in the league, both raw and against those players' averages. Its A-graded frontcourt hasn't translated to defense: Opp Rim FG % is 27th. Denver's best player has a clear path to a big night in the rematch of last week's overtime game.

keyMatchups.title: Murray at Phoenix
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix has been shredded by point guards, allowing 55.5 points a game to the position, last in the league and far above those players' own averages. Its defensive rebounding is also last in the league. Murray and the offensive glass should both feast. That said, Phoenix's own two-game sample is as thin as Denver's.

keyMatchups.title: Portland's perimeter wall
keyMatchups.body: Portland's wings grade A+, and its defense ranks 1st in Opp 3P %, a bad fit for a Denver team shooting 29.9% from deep. Opposing small forwards have been held well under their averages, so the F-graded Denver wings will be under the most pressure here. The Denver edge is inside: Portland has allowed 24 points a game to centers.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Denver's three-point shooting rebounds against three of the league's worst defenses. If it doesn't, the slump starts to look like more than variance.

restOfSeason.body:
Two games tell us almost nothing, so the forecast leans on history. That history shows a team that has won between 48 and 57 games in each of the last five seasons, with a top-six offense every year. The shooting will regress upward toward last year's levels, and the offensive rebounding looks like a sustainable edge given the frontcourt depth. That points to an offensive rating back in the 115-120 range and a final win total of roughly 47 to 54.

Two things will regress the other way. Opponents' 27.2% from three will rise, and when it does the soft interior defense will be exposed and push the DRtg up. The wing rotation is the swing factor between a good team and a genuine contender. Rotation wings with deeply negative On-Off numbers can't hold heavy minutes against playoff-level opponents.
swingFactors: Rim protection as opponent threes normalize
Three-point shooting returning to last season's level

confidence.note: Only two games played. Most rates are shooting noise, so history carries most of the weight.
